cards.explanation: The answer is True. The text says this was after King Jeconiah, the queen mother, the court officials, the craftsmen and the metalsmiths had been exiled from Jerusalem (Jeremiah 29:2). So the king was on that list before the letter was sent. Even the king got carried off, friends.

The answer is Zedekiah king of Judah. The text says Zedekiah king of Judah sent Elasah and Gemariah to King Nebuchadnezzar in Babylon (Jeremiah 29:3). So Jeremiah's letter got to travel along on a king's errand. Free shipping, friends.

The answer is the LORD of Hosts. The letter says, “This is what the LORD of Hosts, the God of Israel, says to all the exiles…” (Jeremiah 29:4). Jeremiah is the one writing, but these words are the LORD's. That tells you how much weight this letter carries.

The answer is False. Instead of packing, the exiles hear, “Build houses and settle down. Plant gardens and eat their produce.” (Jeremiah 29:5). Houses and gardens are not bag-packing words. A garden takes time, and that's the point.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Take wives and have sons and daughters.” (Jeremiah 29:6). He even says to take wives for their sons and give their daughters in marriage, so that they too may have sons and daughters. Families are meant to grow, even in Babylon.

The answer is prosperity. The text says, “Seek the prosperity of the city to which I have sent you as exiles.” (Jeremiah 29:7). The LORD tells them to look for that city's good. Quite an instruction for people who didn't pick the address.

The answer is that if the city prospers, they will too. The LORD says to pray to Him on the city's behalf, “…for if it prospers, you too will prosper.” (Jeremiah 29:7). Their good and the city's good are tied together. Pray for the neighbors, and the neighbors' good lands on you too, friends.

The answer is False. The LORD says, “Do not be deceived by the prophets and diviners among you, and do not listen to the dreams you elicit from them.” (Jeremiah 29:8). The exiles are told to stop listening. A dream that sounds nice isn't the same as a word from the LORD.

The answer is that He has not sent them. The LORD says they are falsely prophesying in His name: “I have not sent them, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:9). Using His name doesn't mean He sent them. A name on the label doesn't tell you what's in the box, friends.

The answer is Jerusalem. The exiles were carried away from Jerusalem (Jeremiah 29:1). The LORD promises, “I will restore you to the place from which I sent you into exile.” (Jeremiah 29:14). The seventy years have an end, and the way home is part of the promise.

The answer is to prosper them and not harm them. The LORD says He knows the plans He has for them, “…plans to prosper you and not to harm you, to give you a future and a hope.” (Jeremiah 29:11). That's what He says to people living in exile. Keep that line close, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says, “Then you will call upon Me and come and pray to Me, and I will listen to you.” (Jeremiah 29:12). Someone is listening on the other end. That's the LORD's own word to the exiles.

The answer is when they search with all their heart. The LORD says, “You will seek Me and find Me when you search for Me with all your heart.” (Jeremiah 29:13). The finding comes when they search with all their heart, friends.

The answer is True. The LORD says He will restore them from captivity and “…gather you from all the nations and places to which I have banished you, declares the LORD.” (Jeremiah 29:14). That's a promise to gather them from all the nations and places. Big promise, friends.
